newsitem.title: USA: New U.S. envoy to Vietnam sees role as bridge.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. envoy to Vietnam sees role as bridge.

text.p: The new U.S. ambassador to Vietnam said on Monday he will start work in early May and his two top priorities will be normalizing economic ties between the two countries and finding still-missing U.S. soldiers.
The Senate last week confirmed former prisoner of war Douglas "Pete" Peterson as the first U.S. ambassador to Hanoi since the end of the Vietnam War in 1975.

"The M.I.A.-P.O.W. issue is clearly way up on my list of priorities," Peterson said in an interview with CNN, although he said normalizing economic ties was perhaps the top issue he would address during his time in Vietnam.
Peterson served as an Air Force pilot in Vietnam and was prisoner of war there for more than six years. He later became a business executive and served as a congressional representative from Florida.

Asked why he would want to return as envoy to a country that held him prisoner, Peterson said, "I've looked at myself and my own personal experiences, my own attributes, and I think I can be a bridge, hopefully, across this river of pain that exists in these two cultures."
About 2,000 U.S. soldiers are still unaccounted for in Vietnam, more than 20 years after the end of the Vietnam War.

"If we have no relations, we'll learn nothing of what happened to those 2,000," Peterson said. "I am very much convinced that with an ambassadorial relationship, that discovery of the fate of those that are still missing will be enhanced. I clearly have a personal stake in this."
"I know a lot of these people, and I can assure you and to the American people that this issue is not going to go away," he added. "I will be working it diligently every day."

Asked whether he viewed the war as a mistake, Peterson said, "I haven't come to a total conclusion. I think there were some things that occurred that were useful out of that event. There are certainly things we could have done a lot better."
Hanoi's Foreign Ministry on Monday announced that the Clinton administration has approved Vietnam's choice of career diplomat Le Van Bang as its first ambassador to Washington.
U.S. diplomats in Hanoi declined to confirm the statement, which said approval was given on April 11.
